originalTitle: U.S. stock futures pare Nvidia-led gains as investors weigh AI risks
summary: Investing.com-- U.S. stock futures pared most of their earlier gains on Tuesday evening as investors weighed upbeat quarterly results and revenue guidance from Nvidia against a series of concerns surrounding the chipmaker.
content:
Investing.com-- U.S. stock futures pared most of their earlier gains on Tuesday evening as investors weighed upbeat quarterly results and revenue guidance from Nvidia against a series of concerns surrounding the chipmaker.

S&P 500 Futures edged up 0.2% to 7,372.20 points, while Nasdaq 100 Futures rose 0.4% to 27,183.75 points by 22:32 ET (03:32 GMT). Dow Jones Futures traded flat at 50,830.0 points.

S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 futures had initially risen sharply after Nvidia reported stronger-than-expected fiscal third-quarter earnings and forecast fourth-quarter revenue above Wall Street estimates.

Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) shares traded 1.3% higher in extended trading after jumping nearly 5% earlier in the session.

Nvidia reported third-quarter revenue of about $115.8 billion, more than doubling from a year earlier and beating analyst expectations. The company forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $126 billion to $134 billion, above the roughly $125 billion expected by analysts.

However, its outlook also pointed to a potential deterioration in profitability. Nvidia expects fourth-quarter gross margins of 71% to 72%, down from 74.9% in the third quarter.

Comments from interim Chief Executive and Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress on investments and financing arrangements with customers also drew attention. Nvidia has increasingly invested in companies that are among its largest customers, prompting concerns about the extent to which its own capital commitments are supporting demand for its processors.

Kress said the company would continue supporting selected customers and data-centre projects through investments, prepayments and financing guarantees, but would apply greater scrutiny to such commitments.

The company also faces growing regulatory and political scrutiny. Former CEO Jensen Huang is scheduled to testify before U.S. lawmakers in December over national security and export-control issues, while Nvidia's decision to exclude data-centre computing revenue from China from its latest forecast highlights the restrictions limiting its access to that market.

Nvidia stock had fallen roughly 25% in November since Huang's departure. Huang said on Tuesday he would be willing to return if Nvidia's board believed his reinstatement was in the best interests of shareholders and employees.

However, Nvidia Chairman Harvey Jones ruled out a comeback during the company's earnings call, saying the board had unanimously accepted Huang's resignation and had no plans to reinstate him.

Although the results provided evidence that demand for its processors remains strong, investors have historically shown a tendency to sell or take profits in the immediate aftermath of some of the company's earnings announcements.

In the regular session, the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 1.6%, while the S&P 500 dropped 1%. The NASDAQ Composite declined 0.7%. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq both recorded their first four-session losing streaks since September.

Investors remain cautious about the broader technology sector as concerns about AI valuations and the profitability of large-scale infrastructure investments persist. The upcoming market debut of Anthropic, the developer of the Claude chatbot, will also be closely watched, with the company's initial public offering expected to seek a valuation of as much as $1.4 trillion.

Monetary policy remains another source of uncertainty. Persistent inflation has prompted Federal Reserve officials to signal greater openness to further interest-rate increases, with markets pricing in a 96% probability of a 25-basis-point rate hike in December, according to CME FedWatch.

Investors will also examine minutes from the Fed's October policy meeting, due on Wednesday, for further clues about the central bank's thinking on inflation and interest rates.

chineseTitle: 随着投资者权衡 AI 风险，美国股指期货削减了英伟达领涨的涨幅
chineseSummary: Investing.com——周二晚间，美国股指期货回吐了大部分早前涨幅，因投资者权衡英伟达乐观的季度业绩和营收指引，以及围绕该芯片制造商的一系列担忧。
chineseContent:
Investing.com——周二晚间，美国股指期货回吐了大部分早前涨幅，因投资者权衡英伟达乐观的季度业绩和营收指引，以及围绕该芯片制造商的一系列担忧。

截至美国东部时间 22:32（格林威治标准时间 03:32），标准普尔 500 指数期货小幅上涨 0.2%，至 7,372.20 点，纳斯达克 100 期货上涨 0.4%，至 27,183.75 点。道琼斯期货持平于 50,830.0 点。

在英伟达公布强于预期的第三财季盈利并预测第四季度营收高于华尔街预期后，标准普尔 500 指数和纳斯达克 100 指数期货最初大幅上涨。

英伟达 (NASDAQ:NVDA) 股价在盘中早些时候上涨近 5% 后，在盘后交易中上涨 1.3%。

英伟达公布的第三季度营收约为 1158 亿美元，同比增长一倍多，超出了分析师的预期。该公司预计第四季度营收为 1260 亿美元至 1340 亿美元，高于分析师预期的约 1250 亿美元。

然而，其前景也表明盈利能力可能恶化。英伟达预计第四季度毛利率为71%至72%，低于第三季度的74.9%。

临时首席执行官兼首席财务官科莱特·克雷斯(Colette Kress)关于与客户的投资和融资安排的评论也引起了人们的关注。英伟达越来越多地投资于其最大客户之一的公司，这引发了人们对其自身资本承诺在多大程度上支持其处理器需求的担忧。

克雷斯表示，该公司将继续通过投资、预付款和融资担保来支持选定的客户和数据中心项目，但将对此类承诺进行更严格的审查。

该公司还面临着越来越严格的监管和政治审查。前首席执行官黄仁勋计划于 12 月就国家安全和出口管制问题在美国立法者面前作证，而英伟达决定将来自中国的数据中心计算收入排除在最新预测之外，凸显了限制其进入该市场的限制。

自黄仁勋离职以来，11 月份 Nvidia 股价已下跌约 25%。黄周二表示，如果英伟达董事会认为他的复职符合股东和员工的最佳利益，他愿意回归。

然而，英伟达董事长哈维·琼斯(Harvey Jones)排除了在公司财报电话会议上复出的可能性，称董事会已一致接受黄仁勋的辞职，并且没有计划让他复职。

尽管结果证明对其加工商的需求仍然强劲，但从历史上看，投资者在该公司的一些盈利公告发布后，往往表现出立即出售或获利了结的倾向。

常规交易时段，道琼斯工业平均指数下跌 1.6%，标准普尔 500 指数下跌 1%。纳斯达克综合指数下跌 0.7%。标准普尔 500 指数和纳斯达克指数均录得自 9 月份以来首次连续四个交易日下跌。

由于对人工智能估值和大规模基础设施投资盈利能力的担忧持续存在，投资者对更广泛的科技行业保持谨慎态度。 Claude 聊天机器人开发商 Anthropic 即将上市也将受到密切关注，该公司首次公开募股预计将寻求高达 1.4 万亿美元的估值。

货币政策仍然是不确定性的另一个来源。根据 CME FedWatch 的数据，持续的通胀促使美联储官员发出对进一步加息更加开放的信号，市场定价 12 月加息 25 个基点的可能性为 96%。

投资者还将研究定于周三举行的美联储十月政策会议纪要，以获取有关央行对通胀和利率的看法的进一步线索。
